Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Ryan Davidson - Commissioner Rod Beck - Chairman Tom Dayley - Commissioner NEWS FROM THE BOARDNEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners July 2025 ADA COUNTY’S PARK AT EXPO IDAHO RAPIDLY TAKING SHAPE A transformation driven by public input and respect for our natural resources No matter what your particular interests are - whether you enjoy being outdoors, doing something active or simply being inspired by nature’s beauty, The Park at Expo Idaho has something for everyone. We’ve been telling you about this soon- to-be-completed masterpiece since the county broke ground in December of 2024. We can tell you that every single person who has visited the site comes away with a sense of joy and enthusiasm. Open spaces are healthy spaces, and this regional treasure will bring joy to individuals and families for generations to come. Additionally, the design features are customized for our unique landscapes, weather and community preferences. The Park at Expo Idaho encompasses roughly 43 acres alongside the Boise River directly behind Ada County’s Expo Idaho property. If you’ve ever attended the Western Idaho Fair, it’s that area behind the horse barns. This once-in-a-generation park will be completed in late summer of 2026 and will feature soft surface trails, scenic overlooks, and more than 600,000 native plants. What Others Are Saying Here’s how one author described it: As cities across the Northwest balance explosive growth with the need for public space, a $43 million project in Idaho’s Treasure Valley stands as a case study in public space reinvestment through transformative collaboration between civic leadership and a multidisciplinary design team. Rather than sell off surplus land, Ada County chose to transform an abandoned horse track into The Park at Expo Idaho—a landmark public space that integrates ecological restoration, destination recreation, and resilient design. 1

The Park at Expo Idaho will also feature a six-acre all-wheel sports garden. So, if you know anyone who loves skating, or roller derby (to name a few) this will be the place. Check out our carousel of photos showing the work done in July. Remember, you can watch progress videos every 6-8 weeks showing you exactly how this area is being transformed for generations to enjoy in the future. WEST NILE VIRUS DETECTED IN ADA COUNTY The Ada County Mosquito Abatement District has confirmed the first detection of West Nile virus (WNV) in local mosquito populations for the 2025 mosquito season. The mosquito samples that tested positive were collected in Boise and Star - near the intersection of North Grenville Place and West Cory Lane in Boise, and near the Star Road bridge over the Boise River in Star. The detections prompted truck-mounted mosquito abatement treatments in the areas surrounding the detection sites to prevent human cases of WNV. The abatement district will continue to monitor and treat populations throughout the abatement district boundaries to control mosquito populations and prevent WNV from being transmitted to humans and livestock. The first positive WNV test pool of the 2024 season occurred on July 12th, and the final discovery was on September 13th. The abatement district identified 27 positive test pools at 19 trap locations throughout the county in the 2024 mosquito season—compared to a historically high 178 positive test pools at 78 locations in the 2023 mosquito season. The public plays an important role in preventing the spread of WNV. To help prevent the spread of West Nile virus: • Drain or dump standing water weekly. For example, dump standing water from flowerpots, planter bases, bird baths, toys, cans, rain gutters, pet dishes, buckets, and old tires. • Ensure that screen doors and windows are tight-fitting and good condition. • Avoid overwatering your lawn and landscape. • Limit outdoor activities during dusk and dawn to prevent mosquito bites. Those are the times when the mosquitoes that transmit WNV are most active. • Dress in long-sleeve shirts and long pants, preferably in light colors when recreating outdoors during dawn and dusk. • Apply insect repellent following label instructions. Samuel Brockway Program and Education Specialist To see where WNV has been found in Ada County in 2025, click on the Mosquito Tracker on the Ada County Mosquito Abatement District website: https://adacounty.id.gov/weedpestmosquito/mosquito-abatement/ Mosquito Division Coordinator Curtis Martin and technician Rachel Smith observing mosquito larvae inside the laboratory at Ada County’s Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement facility in Meridian.Setting mosquito traps Mosquito larvae to be examined 6

ADA COUNTY PUBLIC INFORMATION OFFICERS AND EXTERNAL COMMUNICATIONS STAFF TOUR WEED, PEST AND MOSQUITO ABATEMENT OFFICE IN MERIDIAN Idaho Office of Emergency Management Shares information on Idaho’s Public Information Emergency Response (PIER) Team Public Information Officers (PIOs) and External Communications Staff from around Ada County work each day to keep the public informed on issues of importance in our region. The goal of PIOs and other external communicators is to share the Right Information to the Right People at the Right Time. It’s a standardized protocol for PIOs from around the country. Ada County was pleased to host the Idaho Office of Emergency Management (IOEM) – the state’s emergency management agency - at our Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement Office in Meridian. IOEM Public Affairs Officer Tristan Lewis shared with the group information about Idaho’s PIER Team. The Public Information Emergency Response Team is a critically important resource for the State of Idaho and can be activated during significant events that require public information coordination. Thank you to the staff at Ada County Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement for a tour of the laboratory facility on site. (See box below that explains more about what Idaho’s PIER Team does and why it was created.) Ada County Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement Director Adam Schroeder (L-R) Sam Brockway, Ada County Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement Program and Education Specialist, and Curtis Martin, Mosquito Division Coordinator Idaho Office of Emergency Management Public Affairs Officer Tristan Lewis 7

# Page 8^page=8
What is the PIER Team? A resource within the State of Idaho made up of Public Information Officers and Communications Professionals for all State of Idaho Agencies. The team includes de-facto members who work for school districts, health departments, and local governments. The Idaho Public Information Emergency Response Team was established through an Idaho Executive Order and formed in 1997. The PIER Team can be activated during large- scale emergencies or disasters that require the coordination of public information. Natural Disasters – floods, earthquakes, wildfires, etc. Man-made incidents – HazMat spills, terrorist actions Significant Events – Election night, large music festivals/sporting events Idaho Office of Emergency Management (IOEM) Mission: Guide the State of Idaho in effectively preparing for, protecting against, mitigating the effects of, responding to, and recovering from all hazards. Learn More about Career Opportunities and Ada County’s Benefits Package https://adacounty.id.gov/human-resources/ ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes twelve individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks & waterways, indigent services, juvenile services, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County - www.adacounty.id.gov/ 8
